question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] How do CSS Container Queries (@container) and subgrid solve card alignment issues in responsive design (Variant #1)?
answer: Container Queries allow child components to style themselves based on the width of their direct parent container rather than the global viewport width (`@container (min-width: 400px)`). `grid-template-rows: subgrid` allows nested child cards to inherit and align row tracks with the parent grid container, ensuring titles and action buttons stay perfectly aligned across unequal content.

If not found, it traverses up `Object.getPrototypeOf(obj)` until it finds the property or reaches `null`. Class inheritance (`extends`) is syntactic sugar over this delegation mechanism.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] How does a strict nonce-based Content Security Policy protect a single-page application against XSS attacks (Variant #161)?
answer: A nonce-based CSP header specifies `script-src 'nonce-{random-cryptographic-token}' 'strict-dynamic'`. The server generates a unique, unpredictable nonce per request and adds it to authorized `<script nonce="...">` tags. Any inline script injected by an attacker via stored/reflected XSS lacks the valid runtime nonce and is immediately blocked by the browser engine.
code:
// HTTP Response Header:
Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'nonce-rAnd0m123' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none';
example:
// HTTP Response Header:
Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'nonce-rAnd0m123' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none';

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] How does event delegation work with event.target vs event.currentTarget, and how do you dispatch a CustomEvent (Variant #241)?
answer: Event delegation attaches a single event listener to a parent container to handle events from dynamically added children via the bubbling phase. `event.target` refers to the innermost element clicked, while `event.currentTarget` refers to the element handling the listener. `dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('my-event', { detail: { data }, bubbles: true }))` broadcasts custom actions.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] How do you implement an accessible focus trap in a modal dialog compliant with WCAG 2.1 AA (Variant #321)?
answer: When the modal opens: (1) Save `document.activeElement` to restore focus on close. (2) Set `aria-modal="true"` and `role="dialog"`. (3) Query all focusable elements within the modal (`a[href], button, input, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])`). (4) Intercept `Tab` and `Shift+Tab` keydowns on the first and last elements to loop focus within the modal boundaries.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] Explain how the JavaScript engine traverses the prototype chain when property lookup fails on an object (Variant #481).
answer: Every JavaScript object holds an internal reference `[[Prototype]]`. When a property is queried on an object, the engine checks its own properties first (`hasOwnProperty`). If not found, it traverses up `Object.getPrototypeOf(obj)` until it finds the property or reaches `null`. Class inheritance (`extends`) is syntactic sugar over this delegation mechanism.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] How does a strict nonce-based Content Security Policy protect a single-page application against XSS attacks (Variant #561)?
answer: A nonce-based CSP header specifies `script-src 'nonce-{random-cryptographic-token}' 'strict-dynamic'`. The server generates a unique, unpredictable nonce per request and adds it to authorized `<script nonce="...">` tags. Any inline script injected by an attacker via stored/reflected XSS lacks the valid runtime nonce and is immediately blocked by the browser engine.
code:
// HTTP Response Header:
Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'nonce-rAnd0m123' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none';
example:
// HTTP Response Header:
Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'nonce-rAnd0m123' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none';

answer: A nonce-based CSP header specifies `script-src 'nonce-{random-cryptographic-token}' 'strict-dynamic'`. question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] How do you implement an accessible focus trap in a modal dialog compliant with WCAG 2.1 AA (Variant #721)?
answer: When the modal opens: (1) Save `document.activeElement` to restore focus on close. (2) Set `aria-modal="true"` and `role="dialog"`. (3) Query all focusable elements within the modal (`a[href], button, input, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])`). (4) Intercept `Tab` and `Shift+Tab` keydowns on the first and last elements to loop focus within the modal boundaries.

(3) Query all focusable elements within the modal (`a[href], button, input, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])`). (4) Intercept `Tab` and `Shift+Tab` keydowns on the first and last elements to loop focus within the modal boundaries.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] How do CSS Container Queries (@container) and subgrid solve card alignment issues in responsive design (Variant #801)?
answer: Container Queries allow child components to style themselves based on the width of their direct parent container rather than the global viewport width (`@container (min-width: 400px)`). `grid-template-rows: subgrid` allows nested child cards to inherit and align row tracks with the parent grid container, ensuring titles and action buttons stay perfectly aligned across unequal content.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] How does a strict nonce-based Content Security Policy protect a single-page application against XSS attacks (Variant #961)?
answer: A nonce-based CSP header specifies `script-src 'nonce-{random-cryptographic-token}' 'strict-dynamic'`. The server generates a unique, unpredictable nonce per request and adds it to authorized `<script nonce="...">` tags. Any inline script injected by an attacker via stored/reflected XSS lacks the valid runtime nonce and is immediately blocked by the browser engine.
code:
// HTTP Response Header:
Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'nonce-rAnd0m123' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none';
example:
// HTTP Response Header:
Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'nonce-rAnd0m123' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none';

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] How does event delegation work with event.target vs event.currentTarget, and how do you dispatch a CustomEvent (Variant #1041)?
answer: Event delegation attaches a single event listener to a parent container to handle events from dynamically added children via the bubbling phase. `event.target` refers to the innermost element clicked, while `event.currentTarget` refers to the element handling the listener. `dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('my-event', { detail: { data }, bubbles: true }))` broadcasts custom actions.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] How do you implement an accessible focus trap in a modal dialog compliant with WCAG 2.1 AA (Variant #1121)?
answer: When the modal opens: (1) Save `document.activeElement` to restore focus on close. (2) Set `aria-modal="true"` and `role="dialog"`. (3) Query all focusable elements within the modal (`a[href], button, input, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])`). (4) Intercept `Tab` and `Shift+Tab` keydowns on the first and last elements to loop focus within the modal boundaries.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] Explain how the JavaScript engine traverses the prototype chain when property lookup fails on an object (Variant #1281).
answer: Every JavaScript object holds an internal reference `[[Prototype]]`. When a property is queried on an object, the engine checks its own properties first (`hasOwnProperty`). If not found, it traverses up `Object.getPrototypeOf(obj)` until it finds the property or reaches `null`. Class inheritance (`extends`) is syntactic sugar over this delegation mechanism.

If not found, it traverses up `Object.getPrototypeOf(obj)` until it finds the property or reaches `null`. Class inheritance (`extends`) is syntactic sugar over this delegation mechanism.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] How does a strict nonce-based Content Security Policy protect a single-page application against XSS attacks (Variant #1361)?
answer: A nonce-based CSP header specifies `script-src 'nonce-{random-cryptographic-token}' 'strict-dynamic'`. The server generates a unique, unpredictable nonce per request and adds it to authorized `<script nonce="...">` tags. Any inline script injected by an attacker via stored/reflected XSS lacks the valid runtime nonce and is immediately blocked by the browser engine.
code:
// HTTP Response Header:
Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'nonce-rAnd0m123' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none';
example:
// HTTP Response Header:
Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'nonce-rAnd0m123' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none';

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] How do you implement an accessible focus trap in a modal dialog compliant with WCAG 2.1 AA (Variant #1521)?
answer: When the modal opens: (1) Save `document.activeElement` to restore focus on close. (2) Set `aria-modal="true"` and `role="dialog"`. (3) Query all focusable elements within the modal (`a[href], button, input, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])`). (4) Intercept `Tab` and `Shift+Tab` keydowns on the first and last elements to loop focus within the modal boundaries.

(3) Query all focusable elements within the modal (`a[href], button, input, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])`). (4) Intercept `Tab` and `Shift+Tab` keydowns on the first and last elements to loop focus within the modal boundaries.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] How do CSS Container Queries (@container) and subgrid solve card alignment issues in responsive design (Variant #1601)?
answer: Container Queries allow child components to style themselves based on the width of their direct parent container rather than the global viewport width (`@container (min-width: 400px)`). `grid-template-rows: subgrid` allows nested child cards to inherit and align row tracks with the parent grid container, ensuring titles and action buttons stay perfectly aligned across unequal content.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] Explain how the JavaScript engine traverses the prototype chain when property lookup fails on an object (Variant #1681).
answer: Every JavaScript object holds an internal reference `[[Prototype]]`. When a property is queried on an object, the engine checks its own properties first (`hasOwnProperty`). If not found, it traverses up `Object.getPrototypeOf(obj)` until it finds the property or reaches `null`. Class inheritance (`extends`) is syntactic sugar over this delegation mechanism.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] How does a strict nonce-based Content Security Policy protect a single-page application against XSS attacks (Variant #1761)?
answer: A nonce-based CSP header specifies `script-src 'nonce-{random-cryptographic-token}' 'strict-dynamic'`. The server generates a unique, unpredictable nonce per request and adds it to authorized `<script nonce="...">` tags. Any inline script injected by an attacker via stored/reflected XSS lacks the valid runtime nonce and is immediately blocked by the browser engine.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] How does event delegation work with event.target vs event.currentTarget, and how do you dispatch a CustomEvent (Variant #1841)?
answer: Event delegation attaches a single event listener to a parent container to handle events from dynamically added children via the bubbling phase. `event.target` refers to the innermost element clicked, while `event.currentTarget` refers to the element handling the listener. `dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('my-event', { detail: { data }, bubbles: true }))` broadcasts custom actions.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] How do you implement an accessible focus trap in a modal dialog compliant with WCAG 2.1 AA (Variant #1921)?
answer: When the modal opens: (1) Save `document.activeElement` to restore focus on close. (2) Set `aria-modal="true"` and `role="dialog"`. (3) Query all focusable elements within the modal (`a[href], button, input, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])`). (4) Intercept `Tab` and `Shift+Tab` keydowns on the first and last elements to loop focus within the modal boundaries.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] Explain how the JavaScript engine traverses the prototype chain when property lookup fails on an object (Variant #2081).
answer: Every JavaScript object holds an internal reference `[[Prototype]]`. When a property is queried on an object, the engine checks its own properties first (`hasOwnProperty`). If not found, it traverses up `Object.getPrototypeOf(obj)` until it finds the property or reaches `null`. Class inheritance (`extends`) is syntactic sugar over this delegation mechanism.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] How does a strict nonce-based Content Security Policy protect a single-page application against XSS attacks (Variant #2161)?
answer: A nonce-based CSP header specifies `script-src 'nonce-{random-cryptographic-token}' 'strict-dynamic'`. The server generates a unique, unpredictable nonce per request and adds it to authorized `<script nonce="...">` tags. Any inline script injected by an attacker via stored/reflected XSS lacks the valid runtime nonce and is immediately blocked by the browser engine.
code:
// HTTP Response Header:
Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'nonce-rAnd0m123' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none';

Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'nonce-rAnd0m123' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none';

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] How does event delegation work with event.target vs event.currentTarget, and how do you dispatch a CustomEvent (Variant #2241)?
answer: Event delegation attaches a single event listener to a parent container to handle events from dynamically added children via the bubbling phase. `event.target` refers to the innermost element clicked, while `event.currentTarget` refers to the element handling the listener. `dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('my-event', { detail: { data }, bubbles: true }))` broadcasts custom actions.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] How do you implement an accessible focus trap in a modal dialog compliant with WCAG 2.1 AA (Variant #2321)?
answer: When the modal opens: (1) Save `document.activeElement` to restore focus on close. (2) Set `aria-modal="true"` and `role="dialog"`. (3) Query all focusable elements within the modal (`a[href], button, input, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])`). (4) Intercept `Tab` and `Shift+Tab` keydowns on the first and last elements to loop focus within the modal boundaries.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] How do CSS Container Queries (@container) and subgrid solve card alignment issues in responsive design (Variant #2401)?
answer: Container Queries allow child components to style themselves based on the width of their direct parent container rather than the global viewport width (`@container (min-width: 400px)`). `grid-template-rows: subgrid` allows nested child cards to inherit and align row tracks with the parent grid container, ensuring titles and action buttons stay perfectly aligned across unequal content.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] Explain how the JavaScript engine traverses the prototype chain when property lookup fails on an object (Variant #2481).
answer: Every JavaScript object holds an internal reference `[[Prototype]]`. When a property is queried on an object, the engine checks its own properties first (`hasOwnProperty`). If not found, it traverses up `Object.getPrototypeOf(obj)` until it finds the property or reaches `null`. Class inheritance (`extends`) is syntactic sugar over this delegation mechanism.

If not found, it traverses up `Object.getPrototypeOf(obj)` until it finds the property or reaches `null`. Class inheritance (`extends`) is syntactic sugar over this delegation mechanism.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] How does a strict nonce-based Content Security Policy protect a single-page application against XSS attacks (Variant #2561)?
answer: A nonce-based CSP header specifies `script-src 'nonce-{random-cryptographic-token}' 'strict-dynamic'`. The server generates a unique, unpredictable nonce per request and adds it to authorized `<script nonce="...">` tags. Any inline script injected by an attacker via stored/reflected XSS lacks the valid runtime nonce and is immediately blocked by the browser engine.

// HTTP Response Header:
Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'nonce-rAnd0m123' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none';

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] How does event delegation work with event.target vs event.currentTarget, and how do you dispatch a CustomEvent (Variant #2641)?
answer: Event delegation attaches a single event listener to a parent container to handle events from dynamically added children via the bubbling phase. `event.target` refers to the innermost element clicked, while `event.currentTarget` refers to the element handling the listener. `dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('my-event', { detail: { data }, bubbles: true }))` broadcasts custom actions.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] How do you implement an accessible focus trap in a modal dialog compliant with WCAG 2.1 AA (Variant #2721)?
answer: When the modal opens: (1) Save `document.activeElement` to restore focus on close. (2) Set `aria-modal="true"` and `role="dialog"`. (3) Query all focusable elements within the modal (`a[href], button, input, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])`). (4) Intercept `Tab` and `Shift+Tab` keydowns on the first and last elements to loop focus within the modal boundaries.

(3) Query all focusable elements within the modal (`a[href], button, input, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])`). (4) Intercept `Tab` and `Shift+Tab` keydowns on the first and last elements to loop focus within the modal boundaries.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] How do CSS Container Queries (@container) and subgrid solve card alignment issues in responsive design (Variant #2801)?
answer: Container Queries allow child components to style themselves based on the width of their direct parent container rather than the global viewport width (`@container (min-width: 400px)`). `grid-template-rows: subgrid` allows nested child cards to inherit and align row tracks with the parent grid container, ensuring titles and action buttons stay perfectly aligned across unequal content.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] Explain how the JavaScript engine traverses the prototype chain when property lookup fails on an object (Variant #2881).
answer: Every JavaScript object holds an internal reference `[[Prototype]]`. When a property is queried on an object, the engine checks its own properties first (`hasOwnProperty`). If not found, it traverses up `Object.getPrototypeOf(obj)` until it finds the property or reaches `null`. Class inheritance (`extends`) is syntactic sugar over this delegation mechanism.

If not found, it traverses up `Object.getPrototypeOf(obj)` until it finds the property or reaches `null`. Class inheritance (`extends`) is syntactic sugar over this delegation mechanism.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] How does a strict nonce-based Content Security Policy protect a single-page application against XSS attacks (Variant #2961)?
answer: A nonce-based CSP header specifies `script-src 'nonce-{random-cryptographic-token}' 'strict-dynamic'`. The server generates a unique, unpredictable nonce per request and adds it to authorized `<script nonce="...">` tags. Any inline script injected by an attacker via stored/reflected XSS lacks the valid runtime nonce and is immediately blocked by the browser engine.
code:
// HTTP Response Header:
Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'nonce-rAnd0m123' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none';
example:
// HTTP Response Header:
Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'nonce-rAnd0m123' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none';

The server generates a unique, unpredictable nonce per request and adds it to authorized `<script nonce="...">` tags. Any inline script injected by an attacker via stored/reflected XSS lacks the valid runtime nonce and is immediately blocked by the browser engine.
code:
// HTTP Response Header:
Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'nonce-rAnd0m123' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none';
example:
// HTTP Response Header:
Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'nonce-rAnd0m123' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none';
